flashcard_questions.a: A sketch showing the planned layout of a static media product.
A simplified skeleton layout of a web page or app screen.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a crossed box mean on a wireframe?
flashcard_questions.a: It marks where an image will go.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is placeholder 'lorem ipsum' text used on a wireframe?
flashcard_questions.a: It shows where text will appear without using the real wording.

flashcard_questions.q: What does an annotation add to a visualisation diagram?
flashcard_questions.a: A note explaining a design decision such as a font choice.

flashcard_questions.q: Which element of a visualisation diagram shows the overall size and proportions?
What advantage does a hand-drawn visualisation diagram have?
flashcard_questions.a: It is quick to produce and easy to sketch during meetings.

flashcard_questions.q: What advantage does a digital visualisation diagram have?
flashcard_questions.a: It looks more professional and is easier to edit.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of product is a wireframe made for?
flashcard_questions.a: A digital or interactive product such as a website or app.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a wireframe leave out colour and images?
flashcard_questions.a: To focus attention on structure and user experience.
How easy a digital product is to navigate and use.

flashcard_questions.q: Who uses wireframes to agree a product's structure before building?

notes: 12 cards: 3 term-to-definition, 4 convention cards, 2 hand-drawn vs digital, 2 causal, 1 user card. Each document is carded in one direction only (term to definition), so no reversed definition-to-term cards appear.
